Part One

I Owe You an Apology

Antara,

Before anything else — I am sorry.

The way I spoke to you last time was wrong. Calling you stupid, questioning your sense, bringing in family honour and shame — none of that was fair and none of that was love, even if it came from worry. You deserved better from me and I did not give you that. I understand if those words hurt, and I want you to know I regret them completely.

I am not writing this to continue that fight. I am writing this because I want to start over — the right way.

🌸
Part Two

The Girl I Have Always Known

Do you remember, Antara — every time you got chocolate, chips, KurKure — you always quietly kept one aside for Dadu. Without being told. Without anyone asking. That small girl who thought of others before herself — that is the person I know.

Little Antara — baby Krishna, full of joy 🪔

Look at that smile. That little one dressed as Krishna — full of light, full of life. Even then, anyone who saw you knew — this child has something special.

Your very first birthday — Dadu was right there 🎂
"Art by Antara" — creativity always yours 🎨
The frame you made — "Family. Sweet Memories." 🖼

You made this by hand. "Family. Sweet Memories." — those were your words, your choice, your craft. The person who made this frame loves her family deeply. I have never forgotten that.

Your handwritten birthday card to Mummy 💛
"Mother is a person who teaches all moral values. You help us when we are sick. My Mother is Best. I Love You."

You wrote that, Antara. In your own hand. Those were not just words — that was your heart. That heart is still there. I know it.

Taluk Rank Winner — your brilliance recognised 🥇
RPL Season 4 — you lifted that trophy 🏆
Constitution Day — Nov 2024, your thoughtful artwork 🇮🇳
Your rangoli — every colour chosen with care 🪔

Every diya placed carefully. Every colour chosen with intention. You carry your culture beautifully, Antara. That is not small.

🏡
Part Three

What This Family Has Quietly Carried

I think about our family a lot, Antara. And I want to tell you something I rarely say out loud.

Mummy — waking up at 5am or 6am every single morning. Quietly making my Tiffin before I even opened my eyes. Not once complaining. Papa — sometimes walking me to the nearest bus stop before his own day began. Then I would take my bicycle to college — through whatever weather, whatever tiredness.

Our family — together always, through everything 💙

And then came the accident. I still think about the tears you all shed that day. It was after that — Mummy decided. We will get him a scooter. That decision came from love. From the fear of losing someone.

The scooter puja — Mummy, you, and a family's love 🛵
📅 October 2, 2025 — I handed you the phone with Mummy beside me. Yes — it was me who first said no phone. And it was Papa who said let us gift her. That was not contradiction. That was a family deciding to trust you. That trust still wants to be true.
October 2, 2025 — the phone gifted, in trust 📱
🎓
Part Four

Where Anna Stands Today

Convocation Day — every 5am Tiffin led here 🎓

That convocation gown. That degree. Mummy's 5am mornings made that day possible. Papa's walks to the bus stop made that day possible. Your support — being there, being you — made that day possible.

Science museum — May 2024, curious together 🔬
You feeding Dadu — love without being told 🎂

Nobody told you to feed me cake. Nobody asked. You just did it. That gesture says more about who you are than any marks or any decision ever could.

I cleared GATE. Scores weren't what I hoped — but I'm still going, still aiming for M.Tech. And I remember what you did on 31st October 2025 when I lost my phone — you were there that morning, without hesitation. I cannot forget that. That is the sister I have.

💌
Part Five

What I Need You to Hear

You were aiming for CA, Antara. That showed real ambition and I was genuinely proud. Now it is BBA. I am not saying it is wrong.

But I want you to sit quietly — just once — and ask yourself one honest question:

Is this decision fully yours?

The people we spend time with shape our thinking more than we realise. Sometimes quietly. Sometimes without us noticing. Your circle, your friendships — they are not neutral. They leave fingerprints on your goals, your choices, your direction.

And about feelings — the closeness, the attachment — I am not here to shame you. Those feelings are real, I understand that. But when the heart gets deeply attached, the mind quietly steps aside. That is what worries me. Not your character. Never your character.

You, Dadu, and family — always in your corner 🤝

You are sharp. You are creative. You are the girl who kept a chocolate aside for Dadu without being asked. You are the girl who wrote "Sweet Memories" in her own hand. You are the girl who wrote "My Mother is Best" — and meant it.

I just do not want someone else's presence to quietly rewrite the future you deserve to write yourself.

🏠
Part Six

Coming Home

Completing the puzzle together — June 2024 🧩

Come home directly, Antara. Keep the phone close but use it wisely. Get your licence properly before riding. These are not punishments — they are just space for your own mind to breathe and find itself again.

The rules are not forever. They are doors, not walls. Every door opens when trust is rebuilt. And I believe — I genuinely believe — you are capable of that.

Waterpark — when we laugh together, nothing is better 🌊

Remember this day? All of us in the water, laughing. That easy joy — it is still there. It is waiting. We just need to find our way back to it together.

Raksha Bandhan — the bond that does not break 🌺
Our family — always together 💝

I am not your enemy. I never was.
I am just your Dadu — who remembers everything,
who is proud of you,
and who wants you to be the author of your own story.

With love and nothing else, Your Dadu
